dedupe_keys.name: infrastructure morphology and energy outcomes distribution network morphology electricity use and socioeconomics for 6 280 census tracts in the northeastern united states

description: Infrastructure Morphology and Energy Outcomes is a Harvard Dataverse dataset by Bernat Salbanyà Rovira of Toulouse Business School with 6,280 census-tract observations and 134 variables across utility service territories in the Northeastern United States. Each tract combines network science metrics of its electric distribution network, such as fractality, orientation entropy, betweenness, closeness and straightness centrality, density, assortativity, node degree and counts of nodes and edges, with total electricity consumption, cost and average price, per-capita and per-area values, household income, poverty rate, Gini index, housing age, terrain ruggedness and rural-urban codes, plus GEOID, FIPS and utility identifiers; log forms are included. A companion deposit holds a Jupyter notebook that reproduces the paper analysis. Both are free to download under CC0 1.0 as a TAB table and an ipynb notebook, published in June 2026. Coverage is Northeastern US census tracts. Caveats: the deposit holds one table, and although the page mentions shapefiles of tracts and network geometry, only the table is listed as a file; network metrics are tract aggregates, not a power-flow model. Simulation uses are distribution network topology statistics linked to demand and equity for network and planning studies. Related records: data-texas-residential-space-heating-electrification is another US distribution demand dataset.
